chapter: Leaving home: Fisk, Tulsa, Arkansas City
title: Arkansas City as a bootleg town and the staged raids
summary: He describes Arkansas City, Kansas, drawing patrons from dry Oklahoma and Kansas, and how raids were tipped off in advance and soon forgotten.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: What town was it?
That was Arkansas City, Kansas. That's not too far from the line of Oklahoma. And it's about 60 miles south of Wichita.
: Well, (inaudible)?
Arkansas City must have been about 15 or 16,000.
15 to 16,000, population.
: Not very big.
It might have been a little bit bigger, but not much.
: What made that a sort of lively place?

Well, what made that lively -- you see, there was a lot of people that used to come down there from Winfield, Kansas. Winfield is about 18 or 20 miles north of there and there was a lot of people that come up from Oklahoma and there was Newkirk, Oklahoma, Ponca City, Oklahoma. These little towns. So consequently they had a lot of drawing power, see, because they could get by running these places -- all of this was dry states.
: All dry, was it?
All dry, Oklahoma and Kansas.
: (Inaudible)?
Yes. So people that was wanting someplace to go, they wanted somewhere that they could go to

drink and they wanted somewhere, you know, to meet -- and we just, you know what I mean, and so they just wanted somewhere to go to spend money and these guys were lucky enough, they was able to get off with it. I guess they were probably paying off, I don't know, evidently. Had to be.
Why -- didn't federal people raid them?
Oh, yes, they got raided. But I think it was a nice thing they had going. You know, if --
They had (inaudible).

Yes. If they were going to get raided, they'd call them and tell them ahead of time. So consequently, they'd always let them find a little something. Leave a little something out for them to find and take down for evidence, but not that much, you know, because they was already waiting for these guys, you know, when they come there. "Okay, come on in. Check it over." And check it over and the guys get on back out. They'd open up the next day. Well, they'd take so and so down and take him down for a little while, stay overnight, be right back in business the next day.
(Laughter.)
So that's the way that went on. So I decided I wanted to go back to school, you know, after the club closed.
